svg.aria-label: The backpressure harness comparing an unbounded queue of WithdrawalTransaction to a bounded queue capped at 1,000. Top chart, heap usage over time: the unbounded queue's heap climbs steadily toward an out-of-memory ceiling around 4,096 MB, while the bounded queue's heap tracks the same climb until the queue fills at t≈40s, then flatlines around 1.4 GB. Bottom chart, producer rate over time: the unbounded queue's producer rate stays pinned at its intake capacity of roughly 2,000 transactions per second and never slows, while the bounded queue's producer rate collapses at the same t≈40s from 2,000 down to the consumer's drain rate of roughly 180 transactions per second. Both charts mark the divergence at t≈40s with a dashed vertical line and an annotation panel. Curve shapes are illustrative, not measured constants.

Where the behaviour diverges: t ≈ 40s
Bounded (cap 1,000): withdrawal-intake threads now block on put() — heap flatlines at the settled backlog.
Unbounded: no such gate — every accepted WithdrawalTransaction is more live heap, climbing toward OutOfMemoryError.
PRODUCER RATE OVER TIME — WithdrawalTransaction enqueues/sec (shape only)
≈2,000 tx/sec (intake capacity)
0 tx/sec
never slows — stays pinned to intake capacity
clamped to consumer's drain rate, ≈180 tx/sec
t≈40s (queue fills)
t=90s
Where the behaviour diverges: t ≈ 40s (same moment as the heap chart)
Bounded: producer rate collapses from ≈2,000 tx/sec to the consumer's drain rate, ≈180 tx/sec — backpressure, not failure.
Unbounded: producer rate never changes — nothing ever tells withdrawal-intake-1 to slow down.
unbounded queue — heap climbs to OOM, producer rate never slows
bounded queue, cap 1,000 — heap flatlines, producer rate clamps to consumer
moment of divergence (t≈40s, queue reaches capacity)
